messages:
maria: quick follow-up to the pacing surface RFC. wanted to capture the operational contract tradeoffs and settle on the adapter boundary before we split work.

sam: short version: thin pacing API vs embedding logic in token-router. tradeoffs: coupling, observability, and failure modes.

ken: can you outline the thin API again? i recall options: sync grant call, async lease, batch endpoints. idempotency/duplication was debated.

maria: proposal: gRPC/HTTP endpoint /v1/pacing/{tenant_id}:grant with two RPCs: RequestGrant and ReportUsage. RequestGrant(request_id, requested_tokens, meta) -> (allowed, granted, recommended_delay_ms). ReportUsage(request_id, used_tokens).

lee: if pacing is slow, router should not block forever. do we buffer locally or emit backpressure to clients?

maria: router should have bounded local buffer + soft-shed. small local queue for <500ms of work, past that return 429-ish soft-shed with hint header. avoid unbounded memory growth.

ashley: adapter needs awareness of tenant priority and abuse_score. include X-Tenant-Priority and X-Abuse-Score headers in requests. also support an optional canary flag to bypass enforcement for tests.

sam: good. add trace propagation header (x-trace-id). and an enforcement_level: passive|soft|hard for rollout.

ken: how do we keep billing accurate when both router and pacing can change grants? single source of truth is needed.

maria: pacing service is authoritative for grants. router keeps conservative local cache but must always call ReportUsage for billing. notify/report is best-effort but persisted locally until acked.

lee: that means pacing requires a write-optimized counter store + durable enqueue for usage events. define latency SLA: request p95 < 25ms for hosted; fallback allowed for dedicated in constrained regions.

ashley: fallback mode is dangerous for abuse. plan: fallback -> limited tenant burst pool sized by SLA bucket and recent abuse score. progressively shrink grants if abuse_score high. log all fallbacks for SRE and security review.

sam: API sketch (yaml):
```yaml
RequestGrant:
  path: "/v1/pacing/{tenant_id}:request_grant"
  body:
    - request_id: string
    - requested_tokens: int
    - meta: map
  headers:
    - X-Tenant-Priority
    - X-Abuse-Score
    - X-Trace-Id
Response:
  - allowed: bool
  - granted_tokens: int
  - recommended_delay_ms: int
```

ken: batching: router should be allowed to batch and include per-sub-request ids. the API should accept an array payload and return per-item responses. batching window default 5ms.

maria: yes support batched grants with mapping to request_ids. router can aggregate to reduce QPS.

lee: auth: mTLS + short-lived inter-service tokens from control plane. RBAC restricts which services can call pacing. enable audit logs for grants and overrides.

ashley: telemetry: emit metrics: grants_by_tenant, grant_latency_ms, fallback_rate, recommended_delay_histogram. traces should join router->pacing->model. dashboards and alerting required.

sam: rollout approach: 1) implement adapter behind flag in router (no enforcement), 2) deploy pacing in canary region in passive mode (only logs/recommendations), 3) enable soft enforcement per-tenant, 4) ramp to hard enforcement.

maria: passive mode useful to collect per-tenant decision curves. add enforcement_level config in tenant config.

ken: testing: unit tests for adapter logic, e2e chaos tests where pacing delays/drop, load tests with bursty patterns to calibrate thresholds and local buffer sizing.

lee: ops: runbook should include: how to flip to fallback, thresholds for soft-shed, alerting for fallback_rate > 0.05% and reconciliation delta > 1k tokens for > 5min.

ashley: admin needs: support override endpoint /v1/pacing/{tenant_id}:override to temporarily increase burst allowance with operator_id and reason; must be audited.

maria: billing integrity: if ReportUsage fails, router must persist events durably (local queue) and retry; never drop before enqueueing to durable store. pacing service will also keep RocksDB write-ahead for incoming reports and forward to kafka for reconciliation.

sam: implementation note: pacing will publish grant events to an event stream for analytics and reconciliation. consumer job will reconcile per-tenant counters and emit alerts on drift.

ken: next steps: @sam prototype adapter (1wk), @ken draft proto + schema PR, @lee ops runbook, @ashley telemetry dashboards. i'll collect PR links and sync next monday.

sam: i'll open prototype branch and ping reviewers.

ken: starting proto now, will request schema review.

lee: noted for runbook.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary pacing-service deployed us-west-2 canary-3 rev r2026-10, health: passing :white_check_mark:

maria: added notes to RFC follow-up doc and created stub PRs, thanks all.

sam: :thumbsup:
